rendered: The document reports no squalene production by the engineered chassis strain. Squalene appears only once, and not as a product that was made: it is named among compound classes the review considers untapped potential for this host,[1]longer-chain terpenoids (e.g., taxadiene, squa-lene, β-carotene)[2], alongside the remark that[3]S. marcescens remains relatively limited.[4] The products actually achieved with this chassis are compiled in[5]Table 2[6], where no squalene entry appears. The highest titer listed there for a derivative of the chassis is the sesquiterpene alcohol[7]((cid:0) )-α-bisabolol[8], at[9]102,300[10](mg L^(cid:0) 1)[11]in fed-batch culture, while the monoterpene[12]α-pinene[13]reached[14]32,500[15], described in the text as[16]S. marcescens HBQA7, combined with flux optimization, yielded 32.5 g[17]. So the question's premise is not supported: squalene is a proposed future target here, not a reported output.[18]
